question: What verifiable identity should OpenClaw assert, who controls the signing authority, and which outbound request paths may carry that assertion?
rationale: Static headers are spoofable, while meaningful cryptographic attestation requires a deliberate root of trust, privacy model, key lifecycle, audience semantics, and outbound-path policy that cannot be inferred safely from implementation details.

options.title: Design platform attestation
options.body: Define a core security protocol with an issuer or hardware-backed trust model, audience binding, rotation, revocation, and explicit supported request paths before implementation.

options.title: Expose a generic plugin seam
options.body: Provide only a narrowly reviewed outbound-request signing or credential-injection API so service-specific plugins own identity semantics and keys.

options.title: Decline agent-personhood claims
options.body: Document that OpenClaw cannot prove a human is absent and direct services to standard service credentials or OAuth-style client authentication instead.

recommendation.title: Design platform attestation
recommendation.body: Define a core security protocol with an issuer or hardware-backed trust model, audience binding, rotation, revocation, and explicit supported request paths before implementation.
